Ford Otomotiv Sanayi AS Announces Major Investment to Expand Turkish Production Capacity

Ford Otomotiv Sanayi AS, a leading player in Turkey’s automotive sector, has unveiled plans for a significant investment aimed at expanding its manufacturing capacity in the country. The company announced on Wednesday that it will allocate approximately $450 million over the next three years to upgrade its main facility in Kocaeli province, a move expected to increase annual production output by 20 percent and enhance its role in Ford’s global supply chain.

The investment will be directed toward modernizing existing assembly lines, introducing advanced automation technologies, and enhancing infrastructure to support next-generation commercial vehicle models. The expansion is set to create 1,200 new jobs, according to a statement released by the company.

“Turkey remains a strategic hub for our operations, both regionally and globally,” said Ahmet Duran, General Manager of Ford Otomotiv Sanayi AS. “This investment underscores our commitment to strengthening our manufacturing footprint, supporting local employment, and meeting growing demand for our vehicles across Europe and beyond.”

Ford Otomotiv Sanayi AS, which has operated in Turkey for over four decades, is jointly owned by Ford Motor Company and a prominent Turkish industrial group. Its Kocaeli plant is recognized as one of the largest commercial vehicle production hubs in Europe, exporting vehicles to more than 90 countries.

Industry analysts view the move as a positive signal for Turkey’s automotive sector, which has rebounded strongly from pandemic-related disruptions and is seeking to attract further foreign investment. “This expansion reflects confidence in Turkey’s skilled labor force and robust supplier network,” said Elif Yavuz, an automotive analyst at Istanbul-based consultancy Eurasia Industry Advisors. “It also positions Ford Otomotiv Sanayi AS to capitalize on shifting supply chain dynamics as European automakers diversify their sourcing strategies.”

The Union of Automotive Workers in Turkey welcomed the announcement, noting that it would provide stable employment opportunities and promote skills development in the region.

Local officials in Kocaeli also expressed support for the project. “Such investments reinforce our province’s reputation as an industrial powerhouse,” said Governor Hasan Demir, adding that the new jobs would have a positive impact on the local economy.

Construction work on the expansion is scheduled to begin in the third quarter of this year, with completion expected by late 2026.
